walkthroughs.body_html: The 1559 Acts established Elizabeth as Supreme Governor. The Prayer Book combined 1549 elevation phrases with 1552 receptions, allowing varied interpretation. The Thirty-Nine Articles (1563/1571) gave doctrinal definition. Recusancy laws hardened after 1570; the 1581 Act on retaining the Queen's loyalty raised the fine to £20 a month.

The 1569 Northern Rising and Ridolfi Plot (1571) circled Mary. The Throckmorton Plot (1583) implicated the Spanish ambassador (expelled). The Bond of Association (1584) committed signatories to revenge any attempt on Elizabeth's life. Walsingham intercepted Mary's coded letters in the Babington Plot; Mary was executed at Fotheringhay on 8 February 1587.

Philip II's plan combined Medina Sidonia's fleet with Parma's army in the Netherlands. Hawkins and Drake's harassing tactics in the Channel were followed by English fireships at Calais (night of 7 August 1588). At Gravelines (8 August) superior English gunnery prevailed. Storms wrecked perhaps 60 ships around Scotland and Ireland. War continued until 1604.

mcqs.q: Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.
William of Orange was Charles II's son and inherited the throne.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
